utterances.text: While the witness is on his way back to court, there's a matter with which we wish to briefly deal, and that is this recurring question of how legislation is dealt with. As far as the Chamber is concerned, legislation doesn't have to be formally proved, and it's merely a matter, as we would have said, of counsel, plural, that's from both sides, deciding with the registry how best to identify them, but they don't have to be formally --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honours -- the problem is the stenographer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, before you respond, perhaps for the record I should repeat what I said earlier and that I'd heard you, and I think counsel in the room would have all heard, so I am going to summarise what I said earlier. And that is that as far as the Chamber is concerned, legislation and statutes being public documents do not have to be formally proved. And the Chamber is content to leave it to counsel on both sides in consultation with the Registry to decide how best to deal with them for reference and management purposes. Yes, you had something to add, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Mr. Krgovic is today with us. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Welcome, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, President. Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may be heard on the subject of stipulations, just a quick suggestion. I believe my friends from the Prosecution side will agree because we're preparing a document with the stipulation of all laws. I suggest once we reach an agreement on that document we will submit it to the Registrar, and given the -- whatever P or D numbers, it's -- as an exhibit and that would be the easiest way, I think. I don't think that the Prosecution has anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: No, the Chamber is content to leave it to counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Cvijetic, please continue your cross-examination. Please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please have the document I asked for just before the break. It is 1D00-4992. The ERN page with "General Provisions, Chapter 1," is 0358-3684. I think that's the fastest way to get to the page I need. This is it. In the English it should read "General Provisions, Chapter 1."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see how else to help you with the English page except by telling you that we can only recognise by its title: "Chapter 1: General Provisions." Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please direct your attention at item 3, Mr. Delic. Please read it for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the B/C/S could we move on to the next page because this item spills over.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Have you read this part of item 3 so far?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here you can see the end of that item.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Have you read it? I apologise. I did not specify which document this is. This is the rules of service of the military police of the armed forces. When the military regulations we commented upon came into force, these rules were applied as well. Since we are both professionals, I can share with you that here we see provisions pertaining to the competence of the military police, which is linked to the territory for which the unit is responsible for, or rather, the military police found within that area of responsibility. Do you see that.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Next let's go to item 9. It should be the next page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, it seems that Mr. Delic's microphone is off. I don't know whether his answer was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, may the Prosecution raise an objection with regard to this line of questioning. This is a civilian prosecutor from a municipality. There's been no foundation established that he would have any knowledge over regulations that pertained to the military court or the military prosecutor's office or the military police. Indeed, it hasn't even been established that he's ever seen these regulations that he's now being questioned about. And this is probably not the appropriate witness to ask these kind of witnesses to.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps I may be of assistance before you make a decision. I can perhaps put the question to the witness and that will clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In the course of your duties did you cooperate with the military police?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But you did nevertheless?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wanted to ask this witness to comment on this -- on these provisions since he's a legal professional. The provisions I was about to quote to him is something that he must be familiar with. In any case, he would be the best person to tell us whether he's familiar with those provisions or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution once again raises the same objection. With all due respect, this is not the best witness to comment on regulations that pertain to military courts, the military police, and the military prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But, Mr. Olmsted, the last answer which Mr. Cvijetic elicited from the witness was that occasionally there was this overlap. I would have thought that that would be sufficient of a basis upon which he could frame the question that he is seeking to ask -- within obvious limits of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, I suppose we should wait to hear the questions, but our concern is all the witness has said is there was some, I think it was seldom cooperation with the military police. And so I'm not sure if that's sufficient to now start a whole line of questioning with regard to a -- a service regulations of the military police, which again we have no evidence that this witness has ever read these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, as always, Mr. Olmsted, don't anticipate, let's take the questions one at a time. And if the objections -- if there are objections, we'll deal with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, please read item number 9 to yourself, if you can.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I would like to establish a parallel with the civilian prosecutors and judges. The gist of my question is that there is a delimitation of jurisdictions, but there were also terms of cooperation. You cooperated with certain members of the military police, and here in the rules we find that they can also operate in civilian clothes. Does this remind you of the work of civilian police?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item 9 here it says that the military police can carry out certain duties in civilian clothes. It says a civilian suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, of course. But let's look at the responsibility and the purview and let's look at item 3, and I'm going to give you the ERN number which is 0358-3688.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is page 11 Serbian version of the -- in the e-court, and it's page 10 in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We'll be looking at item 17, and it says in this part - could you please pay attention - it says that -- I apologise. Item 17, please. The following page in English, please. Page 12 in the English version. There you have it. Chapter 3, bullet point 17 says, as you can see in the middle of that: "The detection of crimes and their perpetrators being pursued ex officio within the jurisdiction of military courts ..." Am I reading properly?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In other words, the authorities are identical as the authorities of the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you now please look at bullet point 21. We already have it in the English version, and in the B/C/S we have to move a little bit forward. That's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Look at item 21, please. Could you please read together with me. "The rights and duties of the authorised employees of the bodies of internal affairs in the armed forces are exercised by the authorised military police officers within the given jurisdiction." This rule, therefore, establishes a parallel between the rights and duties of the authorised officials within the civilian bodies of the interior and the military police. Would you agree with me? In practical terms their authorities are the same; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. And can we now please look at the following page. My learned friend Zecevic is going to help me. In B/C/S it's page 19 -- let me give you the ERN number. Perhaps it will make our life easier if I did. In e-court it's page number 12 in B/C/S. Very well. And let's look at bullet point n. Again my learned friend Zecevic is going to help me to find the English version. We are on the right page in B/C/S and now the English bullet point n. And this overlaps -- spills over to page 14, and that's how we will be able to follow the text. Mr. Delic, did you read what the duties of the military police were?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, under n.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, under n, n for New York, let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English version we have to move to the next page for everybody to be able to follow the entire provision. Yes, that's the end of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It seems that -- or rather, does it seem to you, Mr. Delic, just a little while ago we talked about securing trace and clues of this. It was copied from the Law on Criminal Procedure. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's similar. The rights and duties -- or rather, authorities are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now we are not far from the following page that we need to use for my next question. Page 13 in B/C/S and page 15 in the English version. We are interested in bullet point h, 25(h), 25(h), and same thing has to be located in the English. Did you read the text before you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It says here: "Take part in providing security for prisoners of war in camps for prisoners of war." And I believe that I will not need this document for much longer. I just need to look at one more bullet point. In B/C/S page number is 20, and in English the corresponding page number is 23. We're interested in bullet point 7, or rather, chapter 7 or subtitle under 7, the service to prevent -- service to prevent crime or crime-prevention service. I don't know if you can read such small letters.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My question is a principal one. As we can see within the military police there was also the crime-prevention service. This means -- or rather, I'm not going to have any more questions about this document. I'm just going to ask you to agree with me in this. As you can see, the complete organisation of the military police that reflects the organisation of the civilian police. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, when the Law on Military Courts came into force as well as the Law on Military Prosecutor's Offices and when their police or enforcement agencies were established, this meant the beginning of the parallel work of two types of judiciary bodies and enforcement bodies: Civilian on the one hand and the military on the other. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And now we are coming to the point of my cross-examination in this part. There is a problem of the separation of authorities or delineation of authorities. Wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As an experienced prosecutor, tell us, please, what criteria were applied to segregate crimes into categories that determined who would be in charge? What was the first and foremost rule or criterion applied?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first and foremost criterion was whether the act was a pure military act committed by a military serviceman. For example, sentry duty breach, this was only performed by a soldier, nobody else. A bigger problem arose in situations where -- when it had to be established whether the person was a civilian or a civilian serving in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let me stop you here and ask you very concretely. Was the first and foremost criterion precisely that, the status of the perpetrator whether he was a civilian or a soldier?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was a practical matter establishing the --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you very concretely whether that was the first and foremost criterion?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In other words, the first and foremost task of enforcement agencies was precisely what you were talking about right now, to establish whether the perpetrator was a serviceman or a civilian; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me your definition of a serviceman or a military person?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A serviceman, a person serving in the army, or a military person was a person who was a member of the army who possibly had a rank but what was the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: No, no, I'm asking you about the definition. We'll come to the border-line cases. Don't go into that. I'm going to lead you. A member of a military unit or a military, would that be the definition?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very concrete question now. I apologise. We're waiting for the interpretation. Very well. A person who was mobilised from the reserve and was provided with a uniform and a weapon, was that a serviceman, a military person, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, would another criterion be something taken from the bylaw which would be the area of responsibility or deployment of a military unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let's explain what that means. That means that for crimes committed in the area of responsibility or deployment of a military unit, the only bodies responsible were military judiciary bodies; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. And this brings me to another criterion which is the type of crime. There are crimes which are exclusively processed by military judiciary bodies. For example, war crimes by their nature and description, they can be committed by servicemen as a rule, only by servicemen?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So this brings us to a total of three basic criteria; however, this also brings us to a situation in which authorities overlap and you have already started talking about that and I interrupted you. Let me give you an example. For example, a crime is committed. The perpetrator is unknown. Both police forces come to the scene. What would be their first and foremost task? Would it be to separate their respective authorities based on the applicable criteria? Am I right in assuming that that would be the case?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And now let's move to a very practical issue here. You resided in Sanski Most, and I'm sure that you know that in the territory of Sanski Most a large military formation appeared already in the month of April. Tell me whether you know what military formation I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you're talking about the 6th Krajina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I assume that you know that the commander of that brigade was Colonel Branko Basara?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name rings a bell, but I didn't know the gentleman personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Could you please wait with your answer. So you heard of the commander. You heard of the unit. Do you know that within that brigade there was also a unit of the military police?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you cooperate with the military police of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Could you give me the name of the person whom you had dealings with in your line of work?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a military policeman, and I believe that his name was Predrag Lazic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well then.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the Court please produce --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, before we leave this document would you please clarify a couple of questions with the witness because it wasn't obvious to me whether the witness has explained to us that in peacetime at least - because that's what the rule governs, the activities and duties of the military police during peacetime, but I don't know if it is also covering wartime - but in peacetime at least what the witness told us was that there is a parallel function between the civilian and the military police, that they had the same duties, and that the way in which a distinction was made in the end was by the three criteria that you mentioned, namely, the identity of the perpetrator and the nature of the crime and the area in which it was committed. But these parallel functions, did they also apply in wartime? That's the first issue that I would like you just to clarify. The second issue is that you asked the witness whether the concept of a serviceman would also cover somebody who had been mobilised and given a uniform and a weapon, mobilised from the reserve. My question would then be: Well, what about a volunteer who had also been given a uniform and a weapon, if one of the volunteer groups committed crimes whose jurisdiction would it then come under, the civilian police or the military police? Could you clarify this with Judge Delic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will get back to the first part of your question. I asked the witness about the delineation of remit at the time that we are discussing. I asked him about the practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, did you apply these three criteria of delineation at the time we are discussing now, at the time of imminent threat of war at Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I elaborate with the witness, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, but I just didn't see the witness answer. Is that a positive answer to the question raised by counsel, Judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then obviously the interpreters weren't able to interpret in a timely fashion -- oh, yes, and it -- volunteers were also mentioned. Your Honours, I will ask the witness, but I don't know whether he's qualified to know in military rules and regulations, but I can suggest an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there is a category of volunteers under military rules and regulations?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with military rules and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That's what I had assumed. Then we would now have to embark on a polemic when volunteers joined military units and then there's the issue of paramilitary formations, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if Your Honours allow, I will continue with the next question. Let us see document 2D07-0033, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, you can see what this is about. This is a criminal report filed by the command of the 6th Krajina Brigade, and the next subheading reads, military police company, then the military post, the date, et cetera. It says -- it states the addressee, namely, the office of the military prosecutor at Banja Luka. There's the reference to the provision upon which this criminal report is based, and you will agree with me when I said that it's the same Law on Criminal Procedure as applied by civilian authorities. And there are the names and the personal information of the persons who are being reported. Let us now turn to page 2, please, before I ask you whether you know of this case I will say that on page 2 there is a description of the criminal act. That's why I wanted to take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please lower the B/C/S version somewhat and please zoom in on the description of the criminal act right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, from the names of the persons reported and the description of the crimes, can you -- can you see which case this is? And the English version, yes, a bit higher up. I think that the most important paragraph is missing here, so the one above in the English version -- no, no, no, no, no, the English version. So the paragraph above -- yes, it's obviously split between two pages which is a problem. So page 2 of the English text, the last paragraph. Yes, this is where the description begins and continues on the next page. Mr. Delic, do you recognise this case?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please focus your attention on the final part of the document, the final part of it is this page where the description begins and where it says "attachments," which is on the next page in English, page 3 in English. That's it. Please take a look and see what was enclosed by the military police as evidence. It says here under item 3 that the on-site investigation was done by the staff of the SJB Sanski Most; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: On the following page --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn to the following page in both versions, and English too, please. Page 4 in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So this criminal report is signed by Colonel Branko Basara. Let us comment now. You said that you knew about -- you knew this case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Here civilian law enforcement authorities went to the crime scene, but the case was further processed by military authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: From the description of the case and the general information, did you conclude why?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably they had the status of servicemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. I can't refrain from asking you, talking about the criminal report, because you are an experienced prosecutor, and I was too a number of years ago. In this criminal -- is there anything missing from this criminal report which is important for the legal quality of the document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious from this criminal report that it includes all formal elements that a criminal report should have. For example, one that I wouldn't be likely to receive it from the SJB Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you will agree with my conclusion that the criminal investigators of the military police were qualified to deal with activities as outlined in this criminal report?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you about possible border-line cases. In border-line cases when it isn't clear whether the perpetrator is a serviceman or a civilian, could it happen that the civilian police and the military police both say that they have no authority there, and thus, the perpetrator could in a way get away with it? Was -- did you keep that on -- keep that in mind?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we all kept in mind our own remit and authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we're now getting to the part which the other day was announced by my learned friend Mr. Pantelic under rule 65 ter. We received a set of criminal reports or criminal files which comprises 200 pages, and they are not translated into English. Mr. Pantelic suggested how we can deal with that situation, and he made several suggestions to that effect, and he will now make a proposal. From a large criminal file of the military court in Banja Luka, I extracted the relevant parts, and they are relevant because this witness is mentioned in them. And I asked for English translations to be made. Could we please see Defence document 1D00-4907, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I think this document should be tendered if my learned friend Mr. Cvijetic -- previous one could be tendered, this criminal charge which was filed by Colonel Basara. I think -- you can tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness knows the case, he recognised it. And I'm convinced that this is also registered with Colonel Basara when he was heard; and if not, then I would tender this document into evidence. Should I repeat the document number? It is 2D07-0033.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D40, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And if my learned friend Mr. Cvijetic will allow me, I would like to make [sic] a guidance from the Trial Chamber. Earlier before these proceedings I spoke with my learned friends from Prosecution and principally they don't have objections to my application. Actually, Your Honours, we received, as my learned friend Mr. Cvijetic mentioned, we received I believe on 12th of October a bulk of documents, sort of a batch of documents related to -- related to criminal charges, on-site records, on-site crime records, military court Banja Luka proceedings, et cetera, et cetera, against known and unknown perpetrators against -- in main cases against non-Serb population in Sanski Most. So point number one, these documents are in B/C/S language. We don't have English translation because it was disclosed to us under Rule 66(B), I believe, from the OTP, and my suggestion is the following: We could tender this basket of documents for identification -- for - how do you say it? - FFMI [sic] for identification. Then we shall ask our friends from SLSS [sic] to translate it. And then when we got the English translation we could tender it in full capacity so to say. These documents are very important because they consist of many of records signed by Mr. Delic. And simply, we would like to obtain certain comments from him about the documents where he was present, et cetera, et cetera. So I just ask for your instructions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, we appreciate the proposal that you have made to save time by admitting your basket - to use your phrase - all at once. Unfortunately, we don't know what is -- how much at the end of the exercise, how many items in that basket would be of assistance to the Chamber; and therefore, the method that we would ask you to follow is that such items from these -- this number of pages you have as would be according to your case relevant, you could put those to the witness even if the particular document on which you're relying is still in B/C/S and hasn't yet been translated. In the course of your putting the relevant portion to the witness, that portion would then be translated. So it may be a little time-consuming for you and us, but at the end of the exercise the Chamber's view is that that is the preferable course to avoid being faced at the end of it all with a great bundle of documents that we're going to have to sift through and see what we make of it. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As you rightly pointed out, my idea was just in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: To save time --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- in terms of -- to save time, yes. But, okay, I'm perfectly comfortable, we could go through these documents with this witness and then we could decide which part of these documents we shall admit. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Much obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did something similar in order to resolve the situation. I took this voluminous military file and extracted relevant portions. Then I asked the translation service to have those translated. My apology, I don't know whether the fate of the previous document was decided on, the one issued by Colonel Basara. Is that issue concluded? Very well. Then I would kindly ask for 1D00-4907, page 20 in the B/C/S version and 5 in the English. Your Honours, I have a practical proposal. This set of documents is something I printed out for the witness in hard copy. Perhaps it would be easier for the witness to read it that way and then we can follow it on the screen as well just to make sure that we are on the same page. That is, of course, if there are no objections on your part.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, this is another criminal report from the command of the 6th Krajina Brigade, the MP company. As you can see, it was submitted against Nenad Malic. We also have a description of the crime at hand. Are you familiar with this case? Do you know which case this is?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Then we can discuss it further.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the next page in the B/C/S, 21, and in the English, it is page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree that formally and legally speaking, this criminal report is identical to the previous one, that is to say all legal conditions are met for it to be a valid document, a valid criminal report; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We can see that the crime took place on the 21st of December, 1992; correct? What is interesting in this case, which you say you recall, is that the perpetrator committed the crime while not on duty and not involved in combat. He was in a settlement called Stari Majdan. He took two Muslims out of a bar and killed them; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The MP company submitted a criminal report against him; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Because it was ascertained most probably that he was a serviceman; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the document that can be found at page 23 in the B/C/S and page 7 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the B/C/S version. You have the pages in order. This is the ruling of the Banja Luka military court, by which after three days of being held in custody detention was ordered by the investigating judge of the competent military court; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Hence, the perpetrator was processed by the military prosecution authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next have the document which is at page 33 in the B/C/S and page 8 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As you can see, the military prosecutor's office attached to the command of the 1st Krajina Corps -- 1st Krajina Brigade submitted this request to conduct an investigation to the investigating judge of the military court in Banja Luka; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Chronologically speaking we could move on to the next document which is at page 40 in the B/C/S and page 3 in the English. We are still waiting for the English version. As we can see, the investigating judge accepted the proposal of the military prosecutor's office and initiated an investigation against the person involved; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, the same law applies as before a civilian court, that is to say the Law on Criminal Procedure; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Why did I focus on this part in particular? Because of the fact that in addition to the military authorities this case was dealt by civilian authorities as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to page 44 in the B/C/S and page 1 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you see it? This is the scene of crime report.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: From it I see that the investigating judge of the basic court in Sanski Most on the evening at 2100 hours visited the crime scene. In attendance were also civilian crime inspectors, and on the right-hand side towards the top we see their names. There's also a police officer who was on duty and the name of a physician who were there accompanying the investigating judge. You, however, did not attend this scene of crime investigation; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The investigating judge drafted this report on the 18th of January, 1993, as we can see?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Obviously the on-site investigation was done without it being typewritten immediately. Could that have been the case?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And that it was indeed so I will show through another document which is page 13 in the English and 47 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the document. Page 40 -- sorry, page 13 in the B/C/S. I apologise, 43 in the B/C/S, 43. My mistake. This should be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You have it in hard copy. You can read it directly. The investigating judge forwarded the official report to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And thereby you are officially informed of the crime; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This was done on the 18th of January, 1993. Could we next see what your reaction to it was. It is on the following document which is page 39 in the B/C/S and 12 in the English version. Do you recognise your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You immediately contacted the command of the 6th Krajina Brigade and its MP company, asking for necessary information, that is to say whether any proceedings were instituted against the perpetrator; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The following document that we are about to see is yours -- sorry, that is the response from the brigade. Page 38 in the B/C/S and 11 in the English. Mr. Delic, the military police responded to you by saying that they had submitted a criminal report specifying the type of crime as well as other information. Is this what we said previously, that you wanted to be certain that the case would indeed be processed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But just in case, you turned to the civilian police as well. Next we'll go to that document which is at page 37 in the B/C/S and page 10 in the English version. We're waiting for the translation, and you have it in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You are being informed by the SJB by way of a reply to your query that they forwarded some documentation to the military prosecutors; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As far as you are concerned, this concludes the issue because the case is thereby officially transferred to the military judiciary; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In this case the perpetrator committed the crime in a settlement, in front of a bar. Was that the reason why you wanted to know whether this was one of the border-line cases; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you will agree that in some other cases when the issue of competence did not arise, you did not inquire in particular. Military organs could have processed such cases without being duty-bound to report to you as to their actions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I will next show you two documents. First is Defence document 1D00-742 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, when you would have completed your questions relating to these two documents we'll take the extended break.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I just want to go through the two documents I referred to by your leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, do you see the document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This is a report on the work of the crime service between the 5th of September and the 23rd of September, 1992. This is a report of the MP company with which, as you said, had established co-operation otherwise I would not even have asked you about this. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to the next page to see who signed the document and then I will have questions of you. Third page, the third page, please. I believe we should also have it in English. It's the same third page in English. We only need the signature block. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It says here that the report was drafted by crime inspector Predrag Lazic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Is that the person whom you said you knew?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And he signed his -- here in his capacity of crime inspector; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I have a general question about this document and then we'll refer to the text itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to page 1 just before that in both versions. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You can see the number of cases which were processed before the military police company. Let me not read it for you. Look at the document yourself. The Vakuf case perpetrators were perpetrated. Ibrahim Cehajic; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you see that they were processed by the military organs and that they were dealing with the case? Is that the case? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You see that the cases of killed Muslims were also processed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You can see that the cases of killed -- involving killed Serbs were processed. Can you see that? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Radoslav Bilbija, son of Borislav, remanded in custody, I believe that the person is a Serb; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And then on the following page -- could we please turn to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've just been alerted to the fact that the time has come for our lunch break. With your leave, I would like to leave the witness the documents for his perusal and then we will take less time to go through them after the break, with your leave, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, do you have an observation?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have an administrative matter after you resolve this issue. The administrative issue is with regard to the next witness. We understand from the Defence that they're going to be going with this witness throughout the rest of this session, and therefore, we would ask that the next witness be released from the obligation to come to court today so that he can go about his business.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the witness may have the document in the break. We will resume in an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.48 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just explain why I've moved up to the front and Mr. Olmsted's not here. It wasn't appreciated that the witness was going to take so long and he's on a flight to Sarajevo this afternoon which was booked and unfortunately he couldn't leave. So if that's all right with you, as leading counsel I'm going to take over for Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Of course, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, please resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we have the last document back on the screen, and I will repeat the number. This is 1D00-740 -- 42. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, I'm not going to ask you about any details from this report on the work of the crime prevention service of the MP company in Sanski Most. I know that you studied that document during the break. I'm going to ask you this: Do you agree with me that it may be concluded from this short period of time that the report refers to, and it refers to only 18 days of the police work between 5 and 18 September, that the company of the military police of the 6th Krajina Brigade worked very intensely. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can one conclude that judging by the range of the crimes and the range of perpetrators. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And I'm also going to ask you whether you agree with me. I honestly admit that at the moment I can't compare that with your log-book, but in principle do you agree with me that most of the criminal reports and crimes as well as perpetrators were processed by the military organs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to compare without the data, but it does appear that they were dealing with a number of cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I asked for a principled answer. I wanted you to confirm that a lot of your jurisdiction was transferred to the jurisdiction of the military prosecution organs. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You recognise in this document some of the incidents that happened?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. Before tendering this document into evidence I forgot to tender the previous documents, the criminal report that I singled out from a voluminous file which we translated into English and commented upon with the witness who was familiar with the witness. Could we please tender into evidence the previous document which is 1D00-4907. The document was reviewed before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D41, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now since the witness has recognised the events and the context within which the reports were filed by the military police - and he himself cooperated with the military police - I would like to tender this document into evidence. The document number is 1D00-0742.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Also admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D42, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, you were not able to provide a precise answer as to how much of the jurisdiction was transferred from the civilian police and you as the prosecutor to the military police. Let's try and do that on the basis of the following document which is from 65 ter list and the number of the document is 1355. While we're waiting for the document to be produced, Mr. Delic, you had an opportunity to study the document in detail during the break, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your answer was not recorded. A nod is not enough. You have to speak out.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This is a report by the military prosecutor with the command of the Krajina Corps. This is information about crime trends for 1992. Could we immediately go to the first page, the first one after the title page, and can we scroll up a little -- yes, it's okay. In the English as well. Mr. Delic, in the first paragraph already you can see that the military prosecutor's office of the 1st Krajina Corps received 639 criminal reports against 978 individuals, which had been segregated into 742 privates, 28 officers, 24 non-commissioned officers, and what might be interesting for us 184 civilians or enemy soldiers. 124. I don't know what I said, I don't know how it was interpreted, but in any case it is 124 -- 184. Further on, we can move on to the next page in the English version. You have to move to the following page in the English version. Here you can see the structure of the perpetrators and further on you can also see the structure on the following page. Could you please turn to the following page if you don't mind. You will also see the structure of the crimes as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, can I just make an inquiry. Is the underlining or the marking we can see, was that on the document originally, or was it put on by the Defence team? The latter do I see?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I have several copies of the document. That's how it was underlined in the original document and that's how we received the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, I hope that you can find the part in the left upper corner, in the first paragraph, where it says that there were five criminal reports for crimes against humanity and war crimes. Can you see that? Furthermore, crimes against the safety of property. Let us explain. Those are the crimes such as shooting in the air, throwing grenades into the courtyards of religious buildings, churches, and so on and so forth. Is that the type of crime that is described here?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to be sure that we know what we're talking about. I wouldn't go into any further details of the statistics provided by this report. If you have thoroughly studied the document, could you be able to draw a conclusion as to what I previously asked you, that a lot of the jurisdictions of the civilian bodies were transferred to the military prosecution bodies, that there was a high percentage of the crimes that were prosecuted by the military prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A lot of individuals and a lot of crimes are mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Will you agree that in respect of your log-book and in respect of the crimes that you had to process this is much more?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is much more than I had to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, I will now go back to some questions that the prosecutor put to you before I move on to some concrete criminal reports. If a citizen carries weapons for which he doesn't have a licence or a pistol or a rifle, you will charge him for unlawful possession of weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: However, if a higher number of individuals carry rifles in a neighbourhood or are procured with such weapons in an organised manner, then you will agree with me that we cannot talk about a crime that falls within your jurisdiction because in such a case we will be dealing with a potential preparation for an armed rebellion or an armed rebellion?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this could be the characteristics of a future crime of armed rebellion.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And when it comes to the prosecution of such perpetrators it would be the military prosecution organs that would have to deal with that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Even if such persons were civilians?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for that crime the answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. A question was put to you by the prosecutor as to why some perpetrators on the indictment were not processed. I understand that you were shown a list of victims from very concrete indictments, indictments for our clients?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was given to have a look at the indictments against individuals sitting in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. My question to you is this: Is there a possibility that those acts alleged in the indictment were perpetrated who fall under the three criteria that we discussed, that they were military personnel, that the acts were committed in the area of responsibility or in the area of deployment of military unit, and thirdly, that the crimes were of such a nature that they had to be prosecuted by the military prosecutor's office. I'm talking about war crimes, armed rebellion, and so on and so forth. Is that a possibility?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Would that be an explanation as to why those crimes were not processed by your office?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is such a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And now let's just take a perfunctory look through certain criminal reports that you received as a prosecutor. I will not dwell upon them any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown -- I apologise, the military report that we have just discussed -- the previous document that I discussed with the witness 65 ter 1355, I would like to tender that for admission into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D43, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And now let us have 65 ter 1119 for the benefit of the witness. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, this is a criminal case, the title page of a criminal case, of the public security station in Sanski Most. The case was transferred to you. Let me ask you this straight away: Can you tell what the case was from the sleeve of the case? You can see the victim's name?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name doesn't tell me much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can we then look at the following page. Can we open the sleeve of the case and look at the following page. Can we scroll up the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You received this criminal report. You say that it was filed against an unknown perpetrator, and now you're asking from the public security station to proceed towards finding out who the perpetrator was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, this is a customary procedure?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can we go to the following page, please. And can the criminal report be shown to the witness. As you can see the public security station sent you this criminal report against an unknown perpetrator and this page contains the description of the criminal offence, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We've already discussed criminal reports against unknown perpetrators. However, the reason why it shows this particular case can be found on the following page titled "Official Note." Could you please move to that page with the Official Note. Very well. This is it. The B/C/S version is not very legible. Could you please start reading from the beginning of the second passage starting with the words: "On carrying out an investigation on the ground, or rather, an on-site inspection ..." Could you please go through the first four or five lines and then I will have my question for you. Did you manage to read them already?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The inspector of the civilian police - and we will see his signature at the bottom of the note and we will ask you whether you know him - he identified the perpetrators of the crime committed against the Muslim and he says that they were members of the support company and he mentions -- he refers to a name, Dzevar, and I'm sure you're familiar with it, and he also mentions the commander Mirko Stupar; isn't that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: However, he goes on to say that the entire unit has changed its theatre of war and went to Bosanski Brod and that he cannot conduct interviews with any of the members of that unit. However, he will proceed carrying out other investigative work that he can still carry out. He perform -- he carries out interviews with the witnesses, the neighbours. Can you see that at the bottom of the page? And then somewhere in the middle of that paragraph that he can now see on the screen, the inspector in question establishes a link between the attempt to destroy the Majdan mosque with the aforementioned unit. And what I'd like to ask you with regard to this is as follows: On the last page of this report --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go to the last page, please. Skip the following two page and show us the signature page. And could we do the same in the English version if necessary, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, do you know Zdravko Savanovic, Inspector Zdravko Savanovic, who signed the report?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My question to you is: What was then the power of this inspector in a situation like that? Everything seems to have gone beyond his control, even his remit; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And I believe that applies to you too; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So the only option left is for the military bodies in charge to take over; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I see no written evidence of that, so we can only suppose it was done like that. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Your Honours, I tender this document as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D44, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, I will now ask for the following document to be shown to you: 1D00-4646. Yes, this is it. Here too you can see the sleeve of the file. And do you -- can you tell by the names of the persons reported what this is about?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, the victims here are Muslims or Croats. Help me, please. It says Emil Cengic --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we would be speaking about victims of Croatian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But the perpetrators were Serbs, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let us open the following page and take a look at the report. We can see that the perpetrators were Serbs and you will agree with me when I say that they were processed first by the SJB Sanski Most, and I suppose that you too took part in the proceedings. By the way, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The criminal report was received by the prosecutor's office of Sanski Most, and I suppose that charges were pressed. I don't remember the details, but I suppose that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But you recognised the case?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this criminal report and its enclosures as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D45, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Could we now see the following criminal report: 1D00-3142.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let us just check why this hasn't been entered, although according to my information it should have been. But in the meantime let us see the following document: 2D03-0074. That's the one. Your Honours, this is the moment when -- or rather, now we have reached the documents that are not translated and which you also mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, this is a criminal report against an unknown perpetrator. The victim was Tado Ilicic from Kruhar, and I found in the file that he was the same [as interpreted] as Dragutin. It seems that this person may have been a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that here that person is of Croatian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would now ask the -- to see the rest of the criminal report, just to see whether -- or to establish whether it is -- it meets all form of requirements. It reads: "Criminal report against an unknown perpetrator." There is a description for the crime committed and it also mentions material evidence enclosed, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us turn to the following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As you see, these are official notes, and such an official note is usually enclosed with a criminal report about the hearings of witnesses, et cetera, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This is a document signed by you, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do I [as interpreted] remember it? You received the on-site investigation report for -- and forwarded it to -- which was forwarded to you by the police, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And I conclude from this that you issued orders to the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let us go to the next page which contains the on-site investigation report. Is this an on-site investigation report? It isn't very legible.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, you will agree with me when I say that this criminal report meets all legal requirements as to the quality of the process that preceded it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm being informed that -- or rather, I apologise. Let me first also tender this document -- oh, no, it must be MFI'd because it isn't translated. Is that acceptable?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I was under the impression that these -- this batch of documents that only exists in B/C/S at the moment, that what you would do - and I think you agreed to this when we discussed it this morning - was to confront the witness with the relevant parts of those documents and have them read out in B/C/S to the witness. And by reading them out we would get the interpretation from the interpreters so that we would not be required to have them admitted into evidence and they would not be required to be translated. So we would achieve several purposes by doing it this way rather than having them first admitted into evidence and then translated in their entirety. So could you tell us whether you wish to proceed along this method. And could I also, Mr. Cvijetic, now that we are speaking about it, ask you to indicate where you are going with this. I'm simply not sure of what the Court is supposed to extract from or to elicit from all of this about -- all of this evidence about the authority of the various police forces to investigate crimes. I think I've got a pretty good picture of how the lines were divided between the military police and the civilian police, and you have made great efforts to show this to the Court. But if that is -- if there's anything else that you wish to establish, then please tell us because otherwise I think you need not continue to bring us more evidence about this same subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not dealing with the delineation of remit anymore. I have finished with putting forward evidence to that effect. I'm dealing with individual crimes. There's one more case left. I will state the purpose shortly. The point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic. Can I also remind you that apparently you have already used up two hours and 16 minutes of your time, so you -- I think you're required to start rounding up your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am now dealing with issues raised by the OTP. The Prosecutor asked the witness questions about the quality of the work of the MUP services in bodies, especially when it comes to unknown perpetrators. I will be done with this very soon. I just have one more case left, but I can do without because these files are not translated so there's not much we can do about it now. If I go document by document and if I start reading them out, it will not do. So let me just deal with one more case and then I will come to the point of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now, we agreed about the previous document, didn't we, that with regard to quality it meets all criteria?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, then I would like this document to be marked for identification until it's translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Counsel seems not to appreciate the point that the Court has been -- has endeavoured to make this morning, that the question of the translation of these documents as a matter of course is not going to happen. The -- we understand from what had been represented this morning that counsel wishes to put parts of the context of some of these documents to this witness, and I suppose it may arise in respect of other witnesses. And that is as far as it will go. So the question of marking this for identification doesn't arise because it isn't expected that this document in its totality will ever become an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these documents are very important for us and they will be translated eventually. I see no reason why they -- why it shouldn't be possible for them to be tendered into evidence because our clients are charged for not acting when crimes were committed against non-Serbs. That's what the indictment states.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, the Court accepts that in a number of cases where the perpetrator was known, these crimes were in fact investigated and prosecuted. This is not challenged by the Prosecution, and you have presented us with ample evidence to show your point. You have also shown that in cases where the perpetrator was not known investigation was undertaken in some instances. And finally, you have shown to us that the police -- the civilian police and the military police had overlapping jurisdiction in some instances, but that by and large a division was practiced between those two units, that is to say the civilian police and the military police. However, if I understood the Prosecution's point correctly, they're saying that as much as crimes committed by Serbs against Muslims or Croats was indeed investigated and prosecuted in certain instances, then the Prosecution claims that this was done far too rarely. It did not reflect the number of crimes. So in their view, many more crimes should have been committed -- should have been, sorry, investigated and prosecuted. So the issue, as I understand it, is not whether crimes committed by Serbs were investigated and prosecuted; that remains beyond doubt. The issue is whether this was done in all the instances where such investigation and prosecution, in the view of the Prosecution, should have been investigated and prosecuted. Now, you have to round up very soon, Mr. Cvijetic, because we're already stepping over the time that you announced, and we still have to get on with the cross-examination of Mr. Pantelic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I feel like -- it's very difficult to see Your Honour from where I am, but I feel I ought to say that it's not just that. As Your Honours will see, even if an investigation or a prosecution was commenced, quite often that is as far as it went. So it's slightly more than -- it's not that they didn't prosecute or investigate at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you for interpreting my interpretation. But, Mr. Cvijetic, this, as I see it, is what you have to address.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you have anticipated my case and what I'm driving at, but I have tried to use some practical examples to disprove the Prosecutor's words. The following cases that I have singled out show that a Muslim was the perpetrator, and the criminal report was filed against an unknown perpetrator because the perpetrator wasn't identified. Non-Serb perpetrators committed a crime against another non-Serb or Croat. If you don't think that this is within the scope of what we should be dealing with, I'm going to bring my cross-examination of this witness to an end, and I will hand it over to my learned friend Mr. Pantelic who is going to deal with the rest of the criminal reports. Since I don't have much time, allow me to put a principled question to my learned friend Delic about what you have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, you said that in 90 per cent of the cases, criminal reports were filed by the public security station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In other words, in 10 per cent of the cases, and the Law on Criminal Procedure stipulates that, criminal procedures indeed can be and were indeed filed. Criminal reports were filed by everybody else, citizens, the aggrieved persons, organisations. You can personally learn about a crime. You can receive an anonymous tip of a crime that has been committed. My question is this: Among the 10 per cent, did you have a single case of which you learned in any other way; and if there was such a case, was there also a case that the police failed to prosecute?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My next question is this: In the work of the police did you observe a selective approach to dealing with the cases? In other words, did the police process a case in one way if the victim was of non-Serb ethnicity and in a different way when the victim was of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't say that I know of such practices.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My question was whether you observe a difference in their work?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Delic, there is a saying: Everybody's smart after the event or Monday morning court are back in. After so many years after the war, before this Tribunal, before the BiH courts, light is trying to be shed on many cases of crimes that happened during the war, many cases have still not even been detected or discovered. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The philosophical approach which says there is always room for improvement is indeed correct, there is indeed always room for improvement. However, I'm now asking you as a post-war prosecutor. Just help me. When you stop being the district prosecutor in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: When you stopped, when did you stop working as a public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In January 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you have information pertaining to those years, 2005, 2006, 2007, or 2008 about the percentage of crimes discovered in respect of the crimes committed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
