utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the percentage of about 50 per cent of perpetrators who were detected was a good percentage at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you would be satisfied with the percentage of 50 per cent even in 2008, would you not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you compare that with European averages?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have those statistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: A ballpark figure, do you have that perhaps? Would it differ a lot from the percentage that we have here?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the situation is more or less the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And my last question for you, sir: From the sterile conditions, as it were, it's easy to look back at the conditions under which you worked. Would it be overly ambitious to expect from Mirko Vrucinic and the police in 1992 and you as the public prosecutor to have achieved higher results under the conditions that prevailed at the time? Would this have been overly ambitious?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this brings my cross-examination to an end, and I would like to thank Mr. Delic for his cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Prosecutor Delic, I'm Igor Pantelic. I represent Stojan Zupljanin in this courtroom. To follow-up on the topic that was tackled by the Trial Chamber by my learned friend from the Prosecution and the Defence counsel, if I tell you that the jurisdiction of the police entails detection of the perpetrators of crimes, amongst its other duties, and that in terms of the provisions of criminal procedure the police are supposed to service the prosecutor and they work on the prosecutor's orders in terms of collecting information, carrying out on-site inspections, and so on and so forth, would you agree with all that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, my learned friend Ms. Korner is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I have to resolve an issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- as I said, my learned friend Ms. Korner is mixing apples and oranges. The position of the Defence is the following: The duty of the police is to act in accordance and upon an instructions of judiciary organs: The prosecution, the investigative judge, and in some case by the judge in trial. It is not the case here whether a number of criminal proceedings were finalised, meaning they came to the end with final judgement; no, Your Honours. The core case and the theory of Prosecution here must be summarised and focused that if allegedly my client, Mr. Zupljanin, did not act in accordance with the rules of law, with the professional proceedings, et cetera. The position of the Defence is the following, and we are going to show, Your Honour, by this evidence, by this exhibits here to this witness, that the police acted - I'm speaking about Sanski Most now - acted fully in accordance with the jurisdiction and the legislation in force, fully in accordance with the professional standards, and fully in accordance with the instructions and requests from the judicial organs like investigative judge or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I don't want to interrupt you. You're just on the borderline between giving evidence yourself and eliciting evidence from the witness. Be careful --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, it's not the borderline, it's well over the borderline and particularly with the witness sitting here, and what's more Mr. Pantelic did this without even an invitation from Your Honour. I've said this over and over again. It's not for the Defence to make speeches about what their case is or what the evidence may show. It is their job to cross-examine the witness or call the witness in chief. But no speeches, thank you very much, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Following the speech of Ms. Korner, I gave certain informations to the Trial Chamber, so it was just follow-up submission on the basis what my learned friend Ms. Korner just said. So, Your Honour, I'm now -- I'm going back to the documents that I have here that I addressed this morning. These documents are crucial for Defence to show that the police submitted criminal charges against known and unknown perpetrators, that the police acted fully in accordance with the sort of standards of actions and in accordance with the instruction of public prosecutor office and investigative judge. And Mr. Delic just confirmed that. What was the role of the police? It is not the role of police to indict, it is not the role of police to try and to deliver judgements, no. It is not the case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- could you assist me, Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- in explaining -- having regard to what Judge Harhoff has said and what Ms. Korner has said, that are you making submissions as to why these documents that we have spoken to twice should become exhibits or will become exhibits; and if so, it would be helpful if you could confine yourself to the basis of that without, as you have -- as has been pointed out to you, giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Fully understood, Your Honour, but it brings me to another issue. This bulk of documents were disclosed -- was disclosed to Defence on the 12th of October, around 200 pages. So with your permission and in accordance with your instruction it will bring me to the certain situation that I must extend my cross-examination for necessary period of time where this is of utmost importance for our Defence. In all these documents we have exhibits, we have proofs that my client -- actually, to be more precise, members of the police from Sanski Most acted fully in accordance with the law. So I should be permitted to comment -- I mean, this witness should comment certain portions of these documents with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But having regard to the approach which the Chamber indicated this morning that you should follow in terms of getting this evidence before us, I haven't heard a question that you have put to the witness dealing with any particular portion of it. You have spoken broadly about the effect that this -- of this bundle of documents, but have you put a question, a specific question, to the witness because it seems to me that that's the only way we're going to get through this. If there's a particular portion of the document, identify it, put it to the witness. The interpreters will render it in English and we move on to the next piece. Is there a problem with proceeding in that manner?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not, Your Honour. I will follow all your instructions just along these lines, but my idea was just to follow-up the portions of cross-examination of my learned friend Mr. Cvijetic with this particular regard where His Honour Judge Harhoff reacted that it was maybe not related to the case. But our position is it is related. So I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, in the interest of time ask your first question and then your next and go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Your Honour. I will do that. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Delic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have document which is uploaded to the court 2D03-0063.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Delic, let's just be sure of one thing here. The first page bears the number 0048-2336. I have to read all this because we don't have the translation, so this all has to be recorded officially. Will you agree with me that this is a criminal report bearing the date 22nd [as interpreted] of February, 1993, and the criminal case involves an unknown perpetrator for a crime pursuant to Article 172, paragraph 1, of the penal code of the social -- of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the aggrieved party is Tehvid Smajlovic. As a matter of fact, Tehvid Smajlovic is the victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have the next page of this document, the last two digits are 37 -- [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So are we sure that this is correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Here we have the text of this criminal report which was submitted by the Sanski Most police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next page, please, 28. Yes, my learned friend Mr. Zecevic just gave me instruction. Please, can we go to the previous page, 37. Sorry, my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where you see the description of the crime it says: "On the 15th of December, 1992, an unknown perpetrator fired a Zolja into the house which was occupied by several persons at the time and Tehvid Smajlovic was killed on that occasion."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: A Zolja is a hand-held rocket-launcher; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajlovic's ethnicity is Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mirko Vrucinic, the chief of police of Sanski Most, is the signatory of that report; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document signed by you; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You are informing the police station at Sanski Most that you received the on-site investigation report dated 16th December 1992 about that event; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in the final part of this document there is the text of a cable sent by the police at Sanski Most signed by Mirko Vrucinic, and it speaks about the event in question; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a letter written by the investigating magistrate. I believe it is Milena Zoric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is also part of this file; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other persons are mentioned here, Smajlovic, Mujaga and Dzevad --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, I'll assist you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just wondering whether this is going with the documents again out on the public screen because all of this is mentioning victims and potential perpetrators. I think it's been going on -- regrettably, I think it's been going on for some time now. I hadn't really taken it on board. I think it's too late rather than trying to redact everything so we'll just have to leave it. Perhaps if Mr. Pantelic could be a little careful just about mentioning names. I mean, we can see -- I know, because we can't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, I cannot do -- I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here in this document - and you probably can't see it because of the stamp - what it says is that Tehvid Smajlovic was killed and Mujaga as well as Dzevad were seriously injured; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, would it be an idea and would the Prosecution perhaps consider an alternative approach to this, rather than having you waste your time and the clients' time and the Court's time and the Prosecution's time and the interpreters' time, if we were to provide the whole batch of the documents to the witness and have him review the witness and tell us if all of those instances - and you can give the statistics to us, you can tell us how many there are - and then let him confirm once and for all that the procedures here were performed in accordance with the rules. Because I think if that's your point then let's get to it rather than having to go through this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I perfectly agree with you, Your Honour. My suggestion is the following: I will now take another line of questions, and I kindly ask our friends from Prosecution because they provided us with this bulk of document, that in the meantime during tomorrow's session they can provide a copy because all of these documents are in B/C/S language to Mr. Delic. He can review it until tomorrow and then we could go easily, and we shall not go in particular documents, but we shall say okay in general terms, as you said, Judge Harhoff, that would be a practical way, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I need Mrs. Korner's --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- acceptance of this because otherwise we can't do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, we have no objection. The only question is it will take a little time to print them out to give to the witness. Is it intended the witness should look at them overnight for tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I guess that would be the most practical thing to do rather than having him doing it now. And since the witness is going to come back tomorrow anyway, we might as well ask him - if you agree, Mr. Delic - to have a look at this overnight if you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The only question -- how are we to get them to him? Obviously we can't talk to him. We can give it maybe to the witness and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It can be done through the services of the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. We'll do that then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And in order to just clarify to Judge Delic - and we thank you for your cooperation, certainly, I hope you had nothing better on for tonight. The question that we want to ask you is whether the proceedings that were instituted in those cases, whether they were done in accordance with the rules and regulations that were in force at the time. Is that a question that both parties can agree on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course in addition -- and probably like Mr. Delic did it this afternoon -- in the morning -- actually, a few questions might arise regarding the ethnicity of perpetrators and the victims of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I would like to ask then in addition some sort of a statistical review of the material. Would it be possible to have an indication of how many cases are we talking about in that batch of documents, what are the cases about, who were the perpetrators if known and how many, in how many of the cases was the perpetrator known, and in how many cases were the victims known, and in how many cases were there further judicial proceedings initiated on the basis of those criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We'll do our best.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, Mr. Delic, we have these procedural issues to deal with but you understand it. You're a professional. You're a prosecutor too, so this is a rare occasion indeed to have a prosecutor sitting in as a witness, but let's continue. Prosecutor Delic, you graduated from the faculty of law in 1983; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After graduating you worked at a bank in Prijedor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After that employment, you became judge at the municipal court of Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In which year was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1988. In November I came to the court --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. All right. You were appointed municipal public prosecutor in 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which month was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably in late May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me if I say that at the time when the SFRJ existed, including the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, for someone to be either judge or public prosecutor in 99.9 per cent of the cases he or she would have to have been a member of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The role of a judge and a prosecutor in any system is to protect the constitutional and legal order. Let's take the example of the United States, where the prosecutor acts on behalf of the state or the people. In monarchies he or she acts on behalf of the king or queen. And in our country the prosecutor always acted on behalf of the state. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And it is not contested that the Republika Srpska was established on the 30th of January, 1992, was it --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, the interpreter apologizes. I didn't catch the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 9th of January, 1992. The answer was affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the constitution of the Republika Srpska was adopted?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the Law on the Government of the Republika Srpska was adopted?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And as my learned friend Mr. Cvijetic spoke with you about a series of laws and regulations including criminal law was adopted from the previous system and became part of the legal system of the Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And it was fully legitimate for criminal proceedings to be conducted against individuals or criminal groups who engaged in armed rebellion against the authorities of the Republika Srpska. I'm speaking about all illegal arming or armed rebellion or getting together to form armed rebellious groups. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This may have been my omission. I'm not sure how you were appointed in May 1992. Whose initiative was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that a meeting was held in the court building and Vlado Vrkes said that a decision was adopted under which, among other things, I was appointed as the public prosecutor of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In May 1992, were you a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Before May 1992, were you a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Since May 1992, have you ever been a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you a member of the League of Communists before that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you a member of any other party?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the year 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you were appointed by the Serbian municipal leadership as an individual outside any party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For purposes of accuracy, you were appointed as a professional?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But at the time you had next to no experience in criminal matters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And bearing in mind the very quick development of events in May 1992, you were facing great difficulties in going about your work in a professional manner, both with regard to professional background and the -- and all the events that went on at the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Colonel Basara, the commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade in Sanski Most testified here. You said that you know him by name but not -- but that you never met him in person. My question to you is: He confirmed, and there is other information to that effect that the 6th Krajina Brigade consisted of over 4.000 soldiers. Is that information correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible that the figure you stated is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you seem to be moving into another area now, and it is 4.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And just for the record, Your Honour, I spoke with my learned friend Mr. Zecevic during the break, it is not complaint but it's rather a friendly I would say advice or pray -- I don't know how to say. Today we were facing significant problems with the English interpretation which was made by certain Mr. - I don't know his name - from interpreters' booth. This is a criminal proceedings and every word and every formulation is of certain importance. So I would just like to bring that for the record that we were not satisfied with the English translation from Serbian to English of gentleman who was in charge today. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, I would remind you, as I did on Thursday, that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Delic, I would remind you, as I did on Thursday, that overnight you, being still a witness under oath, cannot communicate with counsel from either side nor can you discuss your testimony with anybody outside the courtroom. The -- you may have gathered from what passed between the Bench and counsel that there are certain documents that are going to be supplied to you by the Registry for you to review overnight. So we take the adjournment until tomorrow in this courtroom at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
